sections.h2: Which sale route suits a house in Statesboro?
sections.html:
An owner in Statesboro can hire a listing agent, market the place alone, or sell to a company that pays cash and buys the house as it stands. The choice usually turns on two things: how much work the house needs, and whether anyone is living in it under a lease.

  • A retail listing pays best for a clean, updated house when the owner can sit through weeks of showings and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Handling the sale yourself keeps the agent's share but leaves the contract, the disclosures and the haggling on your desk.
  • A direct cash sale appeals to landlords, heirs and owners facing a deadline, because it skips repairs and lender conditions.

Statesboro covers only about 15 square miles, and much of its housing is rented. Settle the tenant question early, since it changes who can buy and how quickly.

sections.h2: How many Statesboro homes are owner-occupied, and what do they cost?
sections.html:
Barely one home in five is lived in by its owner. The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates give Statesboro an owner-occupied rate of 22.1 percent across 12,545 households, and it counts 35,366 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 33,438 in the 2020 census.

sections.h2: How did Statesboro become a college and industrial town?
sections.html:
Statesboro is the seat of Bulloch County, and the county's own planning document says the area grew in the late 1800s on railroads that hauled out timber, Sea Island cotton and naval stores. The city was incorporated in 1903. By 1906 local leaders were asking the state to place a small teacher's college there, and that school became Georgia Southern University.

The same plan treats the university, now enrolling 25,500 students, as the largest single force shaping modern Statesboro. It describes an industrial surge in the 1990s, when Wal-Mart, Briggs and Stratton and Viracon settled in the county's industrial park. Later the Development Authority bought land along Interstate 16, and the county and city extended water and sewer lines to the Bruce Yawn Commerce Park on the US 301 corridor.

Farming remains part of the picture, with more than 206,000 farm acres in Bulloch County given over to row crops, livestock and poultry, plus newer ventures such as sweet onions and satsuma citrus. A house on the edge of town can sit beside working land.

sections.h2: Who tends to sell a Statesboro house quickly?
sections.html:
Most of these sellers hold a property that would need money or time before a retail buyer would touch it. In a university town the trigger often follows the lease calendar or a landlord's decision to cash out.

  • Landlords whose tenants are still under lease, or whose unit sat vacant after students left.
  • Heirs carrying a Bulloch County house while the estate and the deed are sorted out.
  • Owners behind on the mortgage who want to close before a foreclosure date.
  • Sellers facing roof, plumbing or foundation work that a lender's appraiser would flag.

If someone lives in the house, collect the written lease and the deposit amount before you take any offer. A buyer who assumes the lease will want both, and the deposit has to be accounted for at the closing table.

sections.h2: What does Bulloch County do with property tax, and what matters at a sale?
sections.html:
Bulloch values property as of January 1 and taxes 40 percent of that value, less exemptions, at the millage rates of each taxing body. The county's tax page points out an unusual local arrangement: in Bulloch, the Board of Tax Assessors rather than the tax commissioner takes tax returns and homestead applications.

  • Anyone who acquired property in the prior year files a real property return by April 1, and a late filing can carry a 10 percent penalty.
  • A transferee who had the PT-61 transfer form filed and the tax paid, with no subdivision or building afterward, does not need to file a return.
  • To contest a changed value, write to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice. If the board holds firm, the file goes to the Board of Equalization, and arbitration is the alternative.
  • Bulloch's local page lists the standard $2,000 homestead exemption plus age and disability breaks, and it describes a deferral program for owners 62 and older with gross income of $15,000 or less.
  • Farmland used for farming can be assessed at 30 percent instead of 40 under a program that asks the owner to commit for 10 years.

The Department of Revenue's list of counties with a homestead valuation freeze does not include Bulloch. Its county page adds that December 20 is the default payment date, which a county may change, so ask the Bulloch tax commissioner what date applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What happens at the courthouse when a Statesboro house changes hands?
sections.html:
Before the Bulloch County Clerk of Superior Court will record a deed, the state wants its transfer tax. The Department of Revenue names the seller as the party who owes it unless the sales contract shifts the cost to the buyer, and it publishes the rate and the exceptions on its transfer tax page. A security deed, or a release of one, needs no PT-61 at all.

The closing attorney or title company usually files the PT-61 online and pays the tax out of the proceeds. The county tax offices share an annex on North Main Street in downtown Statesboro, open 8 AM to 5 PM on weekdays. Carry the parcel number with you, because the assessors and the tax commissioner keep separate files.

sections.h2: How do Statesboro's highways and new employers affect demand?
sections.html:
Interstate 16 and US 301 are the arteries. The county plan expects Bulloch to feel the pull of the Hyundai Metaplant rising in neighboring Bryan County, and it names Aspen Aerogels, announced in February 2022 with 250 advanced manufacturing jobs, as the first of five industries heading to the county. Georgia Highway 67 and the I-16 interchange zone are marked for denser growth where utilities will reach.

Daily-life amenities show up too. The S and S Greenway is a 3.1 mile paved trail on the old Savannah and Statesboro railway bed, and Mill Creek Regional Park spreads over 223 acres and has drawn crowds as large as 20,000 in a day. The Census Bureau puts the typical trip to work at 22.9 minutes. When you describe a house to a buyer, mention distance to campus, access to I-16 and what a landlord could charge for rent.

sections.h2: What should a Statesboro owner do before taking an offer?
sections.html:
1. Look up your parcel with the Bulloch assessors and confirm the value and any exemption on record.
  2. Gather the lease, the deposit amount and the tenant's contact details if the house is occupied.
  3. Ask the tax commissioner what is owed and when, and learn whether your lender pays from escrow.
  4. Put an as-is cash price beside a listing agent's opinion of value and weigh the gap against repair costs and carrying costs.
  5. Pick a closing attorney or title company to clear liens, handle the PT-61 and record the deed.

Send tax questions to the county offices and estate or lien questions to the closing attorney.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Statesboro house close for cash?
faqs.a: Timing depends on title and on the buyer. A house with an open estate or an unpaid lien takes longer, because the title search sets the pace and the deed cannot be recorded until the transfer tax is paid and liens are cleared.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer owe the Georgia transfer tax in Statesboro?
faqs.a: The seller owes it unless the sales contract says the buyer will pay. The Department of Revenue's transfer tax page gives the rate, which is applied to the sale price.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Statesboro house while tenants live in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer can take the house subject to the lease, or you can end the lease under its own terms before closing. Keep the written lease and the deposit record, since both are needed at closing.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Bulloch County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date on the notice of change, in writing, to the Board of Tax Assessors. The appeal can rest on taxability, value or uniformity, and it cannot be a complaint about the amount of tax.

faqs.q: What if I inherited the Statesboro house?
faqs.a: You need clear authority before any buyer can close, and the estate representative has to sign. Ask the closing attorney what documents the title company will require, then set the closing date.
